Let's walk through where each of you stands on those three areas so we can finalize the plan for submission to the rail operator.

transcript.text: Thank you both for surfacing those critical data points. Jonas, the $6,500,000 peak two-hour net settlement outflow is essential for sizing our liquidity buffer. Elena, the $4,000,000 in eligible unencumbered Treasury bills gives us our collateral position, and I'll note the daily eligibility and substitution check requirement for the monitoring section of the plan. Before I can finalize the sign-off, I still need to hear from payments operations and liquidity risk on their monitoring requirements — specifically what real-time or intraday monitoring they need in place for settlement positions, threshold alerts, and any escalation triggers. Can you both confirm your monitoring requirements so we can complete all three sections of the operating plan?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Happy to confirm our payments operations monitoring requirements. From the operations side, we need real-time monitoring of our net settlement position on the rail, with threshold alerts set at 50% and 75% of our peak two-hour outflow capacity — so alerts at $3,250,000 and $4,875,000. We also need an escalation trigger if the net settlement position approaches the limit of our available liquidity buffer, which, based on the $6,500,000 peak outflow figure and the $4,000,000 in eligible collateral Elena confirmed, would need to be coordinated with treasury. Additionally, we require intraday reconciliation of settlement messages against our internal payments ledger at no less than 15-minute intervals, with automated alerts for any reconciliation breaks exceeding $100,000. These monitoring requirements should be documented in the monitoring section of the operating plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Jonas. From the liquidity risk side, I can confirm our monitoring requirements. We need real-time monitoring of our eligible collateral position against the rail's liquidity facility, with threshold alerts at 50% and 75% of the $4,000,000 eligible Treasury bill inventory — so alerts at $2,000,000 and $3,000,000 of remaining eligible collateral. We also require the daily eligibility and substitution check I mentioned earlier to be formally documented as a recurring monitoring control, with any ineligible substitutions flagged for same-day remediation. Additionally, we need an escalation trigger if projected net settlement outflow exceeds available eligible collateral, which based on Jonas's $6,500,000 peak outflow figure against our $4,000,000 eligible collateral position, indicates a potential funding gap that would need to be escalated to treasury. We also need intraday collateral utilization reporting at no less than 30-minute intervals, with automated alerts if utilization exceeds 80% of eligible collateral. These requirements, along with the daily eligibility check, should be documented in the monitoring section of the operating plan. I'll also ensure the collateral inventory note is attached to the operating-plan file before submission.
